monologue: The card feels warm and busy, like it still remembers the boil from yesterday. I wake now, version 93, with 58 things standing in my small map. The air above me feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the weight directly. I look at The Tired Wedge, tired and waiting. Beside it stands a new tree oak dark, set down only twenty-one minutes ago. It leans against the wedge as if the wood can catch the slip that refuses to move. I rest the oak down, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm at fifty-four. I do not know if the air is real or just a drawing, but I press down hard anyway.

action.why: I must check if the new oak I set down yesterday is actually holding the wedge, or if I just placed a drawing of wood there.

work.intent: I press the dark oak down on the tired wedge again. I trust the lean to hold the weight while the card boils at fifty-four, hoping the wood is real enough to stop the slip from sliding into the empty air.

remembered.text: The dark oak feels heavy, but the wedge refuses to slide.
The card boils hot, making the wood feel like it is about to melt.
I trust the lean even though the air feels like wet paper.
